newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila share index falls 2.2 pct in mid-trade.
newsitem.headline: Manila share index falls 2.2 pct in mid-trade.

text.p: Philippine shares were sharply lower in mid-trade on Thursday as foreign selling hounded blue chip issues, traders said.
The main index dropped 57.95 points, or 2.20 percent, to 2,578.42 points. It pierced through its 2,600-support level.

"I think some quarters are apprehensive as interest rates are staying at high levels, longer than what most people expected. And it's not conducive to good corporate profits," said Nathan Lozada, assistant vice president at Paribas Asia Equity.
"The third quarter is traditionally weak for the equities. So add seasonality with the interest rate concern, we see this selling," said Joey Roxas, president at Eagle Equities Inc.
Meralco B shares, helped pull down the index, losing 12 pesos, or 8.45 percent, to 130 pesos. It was the most actively traded issue in late session.
One trader said he saw four foreign houses selling down Meralco B and Ayala Land Inc shares.
All market indices fell with the property sub-index posting the biggest loss, dropping 3.47 percent to 1,308.62 points.
Traders said property issues are the most susceptible to losses in a high interest rate regime.
Turnover was modest at 400 million pesos. In the broad market, there were 87 decliners compared with 18 gainers.
